hints.text: Compute maker profit separately for informed and uninformed trades.
An informed trade loses the maker $2; either kind of uninformed trade earns the maker $2.

solution.setup: Condition on whether the customer is informed.
solution.reasoning: If informed, the customer buys at 102 before value rises to 104 or sells at 98 before value falls to 96, costing the maker $2. If uninformed, buying at 102 or selling at 98 earns the maker $2 relative to value 100. Thus expected profit is 0.2(−2)+0.8(2).
solution.sanityCheck: The 80% uninformed flow more than compensates for equally sized losses on the 20% informed flow.

keyInsight: A spread earns money from noise flow but loses against traders who condition direction on future value.
recognitionCues: Customer information changes both trade direction and post-trade fair value.
commonMistakes: Averaging buy and sell directions without conditioning on informed behavior.
followUps: What informed-flow probability makes this quote break even?

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with Jump Trading, Citadel Securities, IMC.

title: A Spread Against Informed Flow
problem: An asset's current fair value is $100. You quote $98 bid and $102 ask. With probability 20%, the customer knows the value will immediately move to either $96 or $104 and trades only in the profitable direction. Otherwise the customer is uninformed and buys or sells with equal probability while value stays $100. What is your expected profit per trade?
